24 October 2026: 60-second constructive baseline preflight
The first native preflight of the constructive classical baseline failed its required path. On the inspected 80-trip engineering timetable, setup and route construction reached charging at 2.204 seconds, after 50 merges produced 30 proposed routes. The fixed charging preparation returned at 20.392 seconds, beyond its once-frozen 8.204-second deadline, before any CF1 optimization or warm full-model start was recorded. This is a preparation bottleneck, not evidence of useful classical-control performance.

The fallback full solver retained a plan with replay-valid bill 3386.201202 and 24 vehicles. Independent analysis checked the physical witness and exact bill; output completed at 57.075 seconds within the common 60-second endpoint. The required CF1 path remained unqualified, so the second recovery task was left undispatched. All failures and spent time were preserved. No model was trained or compared, and no independent timetable or sealed data was opened.

Two repeated full-model inventory scans are a concrete overhead suspect, including rebuilding the mapped-variable set for each variable. Saved events do not identify the exact time spent in each substage, and a late-return check discarded the helper's detailed failure. The next bounded repair is to preserve those diagnostics, hoist repeated work and make inventory checks deadline-cooperative while preserving physical-row checks and the same deadline. No retry or comparison screen was launched.

The source gate passed 61 symbolic/fake checks before the separately supervised metadata freeze. These checks did not predict native success. Preserve the failed source and receipts; only a fresh prospective source-bound attempt can qualify a repair. Manuscript work remains deferred, and the cluster remains untouched.
